scope: One property, one kind of guest

brand.promise: Eleven acres between you and noise.
brand.promiseMeaning: The quiet is the product. Every touchpoint protects it or gets out of its way.
brand.personality: A calm Georgia neighbor who waves from the porch, answers fast, and then leaves you be.
brand.voice: Short, warm and plain. Specifics over adjectives: acres, minutes, bird names. Never pushy, never loud.
brand.paletteSource: Starting point. There is no logo yet, so these four colors come from the meadow, the pines and the pecan shells. Swap in the logo's real colors once it exists.

positioning: A private studio on eleven acres, 25 minutes from Sanford Stadium. Close enough for game day, far enough that the only thing you hear at night is the meadow.
forWho: UGA parents in their 40s and 50s who come for games and campus weekends and want to sleep somewhere calm.
notFor: Groups looking for a party base before or after the game
Anyone who wants to walk to downtown Athens
Guests who can't manage one flight of stairs

foundation.what: Songbird Acres is a one-bedroom studio above the hosts' workshop on 11 acres of meadow and pecan trees outside Jefferson, Georgia. It sleeps four (a king bed and a sofa bed), has a full kitchen and a covered patio facing the meadow. The hosts live on the far side of the property.
different: 11 private acres. No neighbors in sight of the patio.
About 25 minutes to Sanford Stadium, by back roads on game day.
Deer at sunrise and cardinals at the feeder most mornings (from the first two reviews).
Hosts on site but out of sight, with replies inside the hour.
Pecans from the property's own trees.
settles: Lead every channel with the quiet and the drive time, not the décor.
No events, ever, even when asked.
The welcome gift comes from the land, not a store.
Game weekends are never discounted. The quiet is worth the rate.

architecture.why: One home, one kind of guest. A second name or sub-brand would cost time and confuse the few reviews the listing has.

expressions.name: Songbird Acres
expressions.audience: UGA parents on game and campus weekends, plus couples on quiet weekends
expressions.channels: Airbnb, Vrbo, a simple direct booking page for repeat guests
expressions.says: Eleven acres, 25 minutes to campus, a real king bed, and quiet.

architecture.revisit: If a second unit is built on the land, or the hosts ever decide to host small gatherings. Gatherings would become a separate expression, sold by direct enquiry only, never on the stay listings.

identity.nameMeaning: Named for the birds that wake guests up. The name is the promise in miniature: the loudest thing here is a bird.
nameRules: Always Songbird Acres, two words, both capitalized. Never 'the Acres' or 'SA'.
In guest messages, the hosts sign off as themselves, not as 'the Songbird Acres team'.
identity.mission: To give parents a place so quiet that a game weekend feels like a rest, by keeping eleven acres between them and everything loud.

values.means: No check-in visits, no humming appliances, no events. Protect the silence first.
Late checkout when the calendar allows. Short messages that never rush the guest.
Say there are stairs before they ask. Photos show exactly where they sleep.
Answer inside the hour, then leave them be. Help like a neighbor, not a concierge.

guest.who: A UGA parent in their 40s or 50s, usually a couple from metro Atlanta, whose son or daughter is at the university.
guest.trigger: The football schedule drops and Athens hotels are already over $300 a night with two-night minimums.
guest.before: Braced for game-day prices, traffic and a noisy rental full of students.
guest.after: Rested. They saw their kid, saw the game, slept like they were at home, and already want next season's dates.

proof.evidence: 11 acres, no neighbors in sight of the patio. Review: "We slept better than at home." (demo review)
About 25 minutes to Sanford Stadium by Google Maps, longer on game day.
Replies inside the hour (Airbnb response time).

proof.claim: It is what the photos show
proof.evidence: Every room photographed, stairs shown and mentioned in the first message.

moat.advantage: Eleven acres this close to Athens
moat.whyHard: Land this size within 30 minutes of campus is rarely a rental. Hotels can't add acreage.
Fast, local answers and small touches (pecans, bird cards) that a remote operator can't match.
Downtown rentals need party groups on game weekends. Songbird Acres can turn them away.

landscape.offers: Walk to the game, front desk, points.
landscape.weWin: They want to sleep, not queue for an elevator, and pay less than game-day hotel rates.

landscape.offers: Walking distance to bars and campus.
landscape.weWin: They want quiet and don't want a student party through the wall.

landscape.offers: Space and lower prices. Est. similar drive times.
landscape.weWin: The host answers in an hour and the photos match. Few have a real king bed and the meadow.
A 90-minute drive after a night game sounds worse than a quiet bed 25 minutes away.

words.soundsLike: "25 minutes to the stadium. Take Hwy 129 in on game day."
"The patio lights come on at sunset. The deer come out a bit after."
words.never: "Get ready for the ultimate game-day experience!!"
"Abundant wildlife in a breathtaking natural setting."

examples.good: Eleven acres outside Jefferson. About 25 minutes to Sanford Stadium.
examples.bad: Nestled in the heart of beautiful Georgia countryside, just minutes from all the action in Athens!

examples.good: One bedroom with a real king bed, a sofa bed, and a full kitchen for game-day food.
examples.bad: Our stunning cozy studio boasts luxurious amenities and charming rustic décor!

examples.good: We live across the meadow. You'll have the patio and the quiet to yourselves.
examples.bad: Enjoy your own private oasis, a true hidden gem away from it all!

examples.good: Back from the game by dark? Sit on the patio. The only sound is the field.
examples.bad: Unwind and relax in total serenity after an amazing day!

examples.good: So sorry. Unplug the white box under the TV for 30 seconds. I've left a hotspot at the stairs too.
examples.bad: We apologize for any inconvenience! Rural internet can be spotty, please be patient!

examples.good: Next season's home games are open. Book direct and we'll hold the same weekend for you next year.
examples.bad: Don't miss out!! Book NOW before it's gone!!!

channels.how: Lead with the acres and the drive time. Title example: "11 private acres, 25 min to UGA, king bed".
Under 80 words. Use their name, answer the question they haven't asked yet, then step back.
One page. Handwritten card in the host's words. Bird names, not adjectives.
One real photo, one plain line, one fact. No walls of hashtags, no stock phrases.
Seasonal, short, from the host by name. Lead with what the land is doing that month.

swatchRoles.ink: Headlines, text and the dark quote blocks
swatchRoles.accent: One highlight per page: labels, rules, the banner

type.display: Georgia, for headlines and the promise
type.body: Inter or Arial, for everything else
type.labels: Small capitals with wide letter spacing, used sparingly

shoot: The meadow from the patio in the last hour of light
The king bed, made tight, in morning light
The stairs and the luggage cart, honestly
Pecans and the bird card on the counter
A deer or the feeder at sunrise (real, not stock)
The gravel pad and parking sign, so arrival is clear
avoid: Wide-angle lenses that make the studio look bigger than it is
Drone shots that hide the home in the landscape
Empty staged rooms with no sign of life

distribution.rules: Same facts everywhere. Airbnb and Vrbo lead with the acres and the drive. The direct page speaks to repeat parents and holds next season's weekends first.

separationRules: No party, tailgate-host or event language on any channel.
Never list on deal or last-minute party apps for game weekends.
If gatherings ever start, they are sold by direct enquiry only, never on the stay listings.

filter.q: Does it serve the right guest?
filter.detail: A UGA parent who wants to see the game and then sleep in quiet. Not a party group, not a crowd.
"Eleven acres between you and noise." Anything that adds noise, rush or worry at the promise's expense is wrong.

filter.q: Does it pull in the wrong guest?
filter.detail: If a photo, line or channel would attract a party group or an event, it doesn't run.
"Eleven acres" over "private". "25 minutes" over "close to Athens". "Cardinals at 7 am" over "wildlife".

always: Uses real photos, taken in real light
Holds next season's dates for repeat guests first
never: Visits guests during a stay unless asked
Uses the banned words or exclamation marks

footer: Sample guide for a demo property. The two review lines are demo text, the palette is a starting point (no logo yet), and anything marked Est. is an estimate.
